digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler baseline advancement and arbitration
propositions: The reconciler advances the baseline from the pass-START snapshot before the outbound apply, leaving it holding the OLD value when rebar itself pushes a status to Jira, creating a one-pass window where local==baseline incorrectly signals 'local unchanged'.

An operator's local status reopen (closed→open or in_progress→open) is silently reverted by inbound write when it occurs in the window after rebar's own outbound push of a status and before baseline advance, because the stale baseline matches the reverted local value and suppresses outbound.

The observed clobbering (status reverted, description survived) is due to status equaling the stale baseline so outbound stood down, while description differed so it was pushed—not a revision rollback or event ordering issue.

A status transition can soft-fail (IllegalTransitionError caught by backstop) while the pass still exits 0, so advancing baseline on 'pass ran' would record a sync that never happened and make rebar believe local and Jira agree when they do not.

The fix must overlay confirmed outbound mutation values onto the fetch snapshot before set_baseline records it, gated on per-mutation success not pass exit code, to make baseline mean last-synced instead of last-fetched.

The same ABA exposure exists for all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary/description/priority/status/assignee) because all share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard, but assignee-resolved via accountId fast path will safely fall back to local-wins rather than fabricate an identity.
